html:
The Dadi Dadi, also called Tatitati, are an Aboriginal people of the middle Murray River, with country along its southern bank in what is now northwest Victoria, around Robinvale and Euston.

Like other Murray peoples, they lived from the river's fish, mussels and birds, and built canoes from the bark of river red gums. Neighbours on the map include the Kureinji and Muthi Muthi to the north and the Wadi Wadi and Latje Latje nearby. Squatters took up the river frontage in the 1840s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
